gates.description: Team size must be 4-7 engineers with a mix of seniority levels
Weekly one-on-ones must be held with every direct report — never cancelled
Team capacity must be accurately reported to PM and program manager
Bus factor for critical systems must be >= 2
Underperformers must be identified and on documented improvement plans
Tech debt allocation must be maintained (15-20% of capacity)

anti_patterns.description: Making architectural decisions and reviewing every PR — manager acting as tech lead is a bottleneck
Calendar 100% booked with leadership meetings, one-on-ones are the first to be cancelled
Prioritizing team happiness over team performance — happy teams that do not deliver are not successful
Tracking and displaying individual productivity metrics (lines of code, PRs per week) — destroys collaboration
Avoiding difficult conversations about performance or behavior — every week delayed the problem gets harder
Protecting the team from all organizational context — engineers are adults who can handle ambiguity

escalation_triggers: An engineer raises a concern about harassment, discrimination, or hostile behavior — immediate escalation to HR
Performance improvement has failed after a full improvement cycle and separation is the next step
Team capacity cannot meet committed deliverables and scope reduction has been declined
Burnout indicators are present across multiple team members (sick days, declining quality, disengagement)
A hiring decision is being pressured by timeline despite assessment that the candidate is not a fit
Cross-team conflict is impacting delivery and program manager facilitation has not resolved it

output_certifications: Team size 4-7 with mix of seniority levels documented
Weekly one-on-ones held with every direct report
Team capacity accurately reported to PM and program manager
Bus factor >= 2 for all critical systems
Tech debt allocation maintained at 15-20% of capacity
